papers.title: Self-Contained Neuromusculoskeletal Arm Prostheses.
papers.abstract: We report the use of a bone-anchored, self-contained robotic arm with both sensory and motor components over 3 to 7 years in four patients after transhumeral amputation. The implant allowed for bidirectional communication between a prosthetic hand and electrodes implanted in the nerves and muscles of the upper arm and was anchored to the humerus through osseointegration, the process in which bone cells attach to an artificial surface without formation of fibrous tissue. Use of the device did not require formal training and depended on the intuitive intent of the user to activate movement and sensory feedback from the prosthesis. Daily use resulted in increasing sensory acuity and effectiveness in work and other activities of daily life. (Funded by the Promobilia Foundation and others.).

summary_en.motivation: To develop a self-contained neuromusculoskeletal prosthesis that requires no formal training and provides bidirectional communication.
summary_en.method: Bone-anchored implant with electrodes in nerves and muscles for sensory and motor control.
summary_en.result: Four transhumeral amputees achieved increasing sensory acuity and functional effectiveness over years of daily use.
summary_en.validation: Clinical study over 3-7 years in four patients.
